_about: Field terms for F62, same shape as papers/glossary.json.

memorability.definition: the share of viewers who correctly recognise a photograph as a repeat when it comes round again in a stream of images, corrected for false alarms; it is a property measured per image across many viewers
memorability.excludes: how well one person remembers, memory over days or years, and how much viewers like the image

oklab-lightness.definition: how light or dark a colour appears on a scale built to match human judgement, here averaged over every pixel of the image
oklab-lightness.excludes: physical light intensity, and contrast between parts of the image

chroma.definition: how far a colour is from grey at the same lightness, here the mean distance from the grey axis in OKLab over the image; our measure of saturation
chroma.excludes: hue, which says which colour it is, and lightness

cct.definition: the temperature in kelvin of the glowing body whose colour is closest to a given colour; low values look warm and orange, high values look cool and blue. Here it is computed from the image's mean colour
cct.excludes: the temperature of anything in the scene, and the white balance setting of the camera

held-out-r2.definition: the share of the variation in a quantity that a model predicts on data it was not fitted to; 1 is perfect, 0 is no better than predicting the average, and it can fall below 0
held-out-r2.excludes: R2 computed on the same data used to fit the model, which rises whenever a variable is added

benjamini-hochberg.definition: an adjustment of a set of p values that holds the expected share of false discoveries among the results called significant at a chosen level
benjamini-hochberg.excludes: a guarantee that no result in the set is a false discovery
